summary: The current Status::SetPayload implementation appears to mutate an existing shared StatusRep directly, which can explain the copy-assignment and equality failures. The erase failures remain unexplained because the available excerpt omits the StatusRep cloning and full erase behavior.
hypotheses: Status::SetPayload bypasses copy-on-write for non-inlined statuses, so changing a copied status can change its source and make distinct statuses compare equal.
StatusRep::CloneAndUnref or ErasePayload mishandles a shared rep or its payload storage, causing erasure from a copy to remove the source payload too.
